questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was one of the few european destinations available that I found interesting

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty alright, the host university gave a lot of information before arrival -  although there were not a lot of information about finding housing outside of the accommodations offered by the host uni

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Information about courses, introduction at the faculty and schedules etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was extremely difficult, there is way more people searching for rooms apartments than landlords renting it out

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The host university only offers accommodation to 50% of exchange students so there is a chance of having to find something on your own - which is really difficult. So look for it a long time in advance and be patient

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There is two registration portals which is kind of confusing - but I think that they were to change it to one for the next semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a course manual which was pretty helpful, but there was no information about whether courses overlap

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was accepted on all the courses i registred for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't panic if you don't get registred on a course - there is a few rounds of applying so you will end up getting something

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Pretty similar to the danish level but maybe slightly below it.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching were pretty similar in terms of it being divided into lectures and seminars (working groups), but exams were very different (almost only multiple choice and open ended question, were you are supposed to remember pretty specific details in litarature)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Urban planning: Contesting the city
Topic All things media? Emerging communication technologies and their impact on us and society
Global Digital Cultures: Interdisciplinary Perspectives
Environment & International Sustainable Development

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend "Global Digital Cultures: Interdisciplinary Perspectives" because it is interesting to get a interdisciplinary (media studies, geography, political science, sociology) perspective on a specific topic, in this case the digital world in a global context

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Cultural expenses (museums, festivals etc.) - there is a lot of stuff to do and they are not always cheap!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and drinking can be done pretty cheap if you want to

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Through the Erasmus programme, there is a lot of arrangements, parties, social activities and athletic opportunities with other exchange students - and besides that the city is filled with cool places to go out and enjoy cultural and social events

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the exchange parties arranged by Erasmus, its a great way to meet fellow exchange students - also go to all the recommended museums and go explore the nightlife; Amsterdam has a lot to offer in terms of that

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go visit the museums at Museumsplein (van gogh, moco, stadelijk etc.) and go watch a Ajax match if you are into football.
Also go to Utrecht, its nice!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Amsterdam is pretty similar to Copenhagen.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Its not necessarily easy to get local friends, but it is definitely possible if you approach them during your courses, or meet them on a night out

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really - only difficult thing to adapt to is the fact that you are kind of forced to approach and seek relationships

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Its a chill vibe overall, and the city offers everything for any type of people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Apply for accommodation through the host uni - I didn't do it, and was living like a nomad for the first 3 weeks!
2. Make an effort to make new relationships, and invest in the people that you get a long with. Met a lot of people the first couple of weeks that I didn't see again until the end because i didn't feel like I needed to make an effort. But those relations come in handy in the end though
3. Enjoy all that the city offers, try different bars/clubs and go to all the museums - then you can get choose your usual hangout spots sooner. And also enjoy the summer, it is crazy good in Amsterdam!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go visit other cities nearby - you have great options within a couple of hours by bus in both the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany and France

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people, getting out of your comfort zone in periods and being able to live in a great city that offers something different than you are used to

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing - if you are a male student, it might seem impossible so try and see if you can find something with someone else (apply as a couple, it works!)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
